PRIMARY COLLAPSE OBSERVATION: T=64 (tool's actual -w ceiling) with default GPU slot pool. ~16x slower than T=32 (245s in the paper's original suite). GPU utilisation collapsed to 1.6% avg (from 26.5% at T=32). v3 suffix: two earlier attempts (t64s8, t64s8_v2) were invalidated by a disk-space exhaustion artifact on /dev/md0 from accumulated test output (own testing-methodology error, not a code bug); this is the clean rerun with disk-space monitoring.
Rule-out test 1/3: FASTP_GPU_SLOTS=32 at T=64. Wall time identical to t64s8v3 (3969s both) -> rules out GPU slot count as the cause.
Rule-out test 2/3: FASTP_COMPRESSORS=8 at T=64 (reduces live threads from 141 to 93, well under the host's 128 cores). No material change (3965s vs 3969s) -> rules out compressor thread count.
POST-FIX RESULT (CPU build): packInMemLimit() scaling (max(64,threads*4)) + condition-variable waitForData() applied. 3969s -> 238s, matching T=32 (234s).
POST-FIX RESULT (GPU build): >3600s (timeout, never completed pre-fix) -> 240s, matching T=32 GPU (242s).
Regression check: T=32 after the fix, 234s vs the original paper baseline of 241.289s -> no regression (within run-to-run noise).
Spot check: T=8 after the fix. packInMemLimit(8) = max(64,8*4) = 64, identical to the pre-fix constant, so T=8 is mathematically unaffected by the change; this run confirms it empirically.
